# Galactocele

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Obstetrics/gynecology > Breast disorders > Galactocele*

[Original Article Link](/library/Qt0uW3)

---

## Summary

Galactoceles are milk retention cysts that primarily occur during or shortly after lactation. The typical presentation includes a firm nontender or mildly tender <u>breast mass</u>. <u>Ultrasound</u> is the preferred modality to evaluate <u>palpable breast masses</u> in lactating patients. Galactoceles have a variable appearance on <u>ultrasound</u>, ranging from a simple <u>anechoic</u> cyst to a mass with internal echoes. <u>Mammography</u> may be required to evaluate inconclusive <u>ultrasound</u> findings; detection of an oil-fluid cyst is <u>pathognomonic</u> for galactoceles. Asymptomatic galactoceles typically regress and can be managed expectantly. Symptomatic galactoceles often require <u>fine needle aspiration</u> and drainage catheter placement, and in the case of infection, <u>antibiotic therapy</u>. See also “<u>Breast abscess</u>.”

---

## Epidemiology

* Frequently occurs during or after lactation  [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)

* Most common benign <u>breast</u> lesion in lactating women who have recently stopped <u>breast feeding</u> [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)[[3]](/library/O51I4h0)




Epidemiological data refers to the US, unless otherwise specified.

---

## Pathophysiology

Obstruction of <u>lactiferous duct</u> → distention of the duct due to collection of milk and <u>epithelial</u> cells → cyst formation

---

## Clinical features

* Firm, nontender mass, typically located in the subareolar region

* Size may fluctuate (e.g., decrease in size after <u>breastfeeding</u>) [[4]](/library/qh1CUg0)

* Severe <u>pain</u> and systemic signs suggest secondary infection.

---

## Diagnosis

The diagnosis is primarily clinical and based on the patient's history and clinical presentation. A <u>palpable breast mass</u> always requires further evaluation. [[3]](/library/O51I4h0)[[5]](/library/Qe1uAf0)[[6]](/library/Sm1yUh0)




### <u>Breast</u> imaging




#### <u>Breast ultrasound</u>




* Indications: first-line imaging modality for evaluation of a <u>palpable breast mass</u> or focal <u>pain</u> in pregnant and lactating women  [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)[[6]](/library/Sm1yUh0)

* Findings are variable and include:  [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)[[7]](/library/jm1_2h0)

* <u>Anechoic</u> <u>simple breast cyst</u> with <u>posterior acoustic enhancement</u> [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)

* Mass with variable <u>echogenicity</u> and internal echoes (but no vascular flow) [[7]](/library/jm1_2h0)

* <u>Fat-fluid level</u>  [[3]](/library/O51I4h0)

* Irregular borders and wall thickening [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)[[7]](/library/jm1_2h0)

#### <u>Mammography</u>




* Indications [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)[[6]](/library/Sm1yUh0)

* Second-line imaging modality in lactating (or pregnant) women with a <u>palpable breast mass</u> and a negative or equivocal <u>ultrasound</u>

* As an adjunct to <u>ultrasound</u> to further evaluate concerning features

* Findings [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)

* Well-defined mass

* Depending on the fat and fluid content within the mass, the following features may be seen: [[3]](/library/O51I4h0)

* Fat-fluid level

* Uniformly <u>radiolucent</u> mass

* Heterogeneous density





### Imaging-guided <u>fine needle aspiration</u> [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)




* Indications [[3]](/library/O51I4h0)[[7]](/library/jm1_2h0)

* Diagnostic uncertainty or suspicious findings on imaging

* Possible infection

* Bothersome symptoms (e.g., <u>pain</u>, swelling)

* Findings: milky <u>aspirate</u> [[2]](/library/3m1S2h0)

* Complications: <u>milk fistula</u>  [[3]](/library/O51I4h0)[[6]](/library/Sm1yUh0)[[8]](/library/Kg1UwT0)

---

## Treatment

### Asymptomatic galactoceles




* Surveillance with <u>clinical examination</u> and/or imaging [[9]](/library/Rm1l2h0)

* Treatment is usually unnecessary (most galactoceles resolve spontaneously). [[7]](/library/jm1_2h0)[[10]](/library/oE109i0)





### Symptomatic galactoceles [[4]](/library/qh1CUg0)[[10]](/library/oE109i0)




* Needle <u>aspiration</u>: for symptomatic relief (and additional diagnostic confirmation)

* Drainage catheter placement: often recommended to facilitate fluid removal

* <u>Empiric antibiotic therapy for breast infections</u>: indicated for infected galactoceles [[3]](/library/O51I4h0)[[4]](/library/qh1CUg0)[[10]](/library/oE109i0)





> [!TIP]
> Repeated needle <u>aspiration</u> increases the risk of infection but is typically required before a galactocele fully resolves. The placement of a catheter to allow continued drainage facilitates resolution. [[4]](/library/qh1CUg0)

---

## Prognosis

* Usually good

* No increased risk of subsequent <u>breast cancer</u>

---
